turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c012, c047, c003, c031,
c088".
turns.answer_text:
The highest fatigue strengths in the training data are concentrated in the special 930°C process route with CT ≈ 930, DT ≈ 850–896, short/high-temperature cooling/holding parameters, and low tempering temperature TT = 160–200. These rows reach about 1000–1144 MPa, well above the conventional heat-treatment groups and the high-Si 845°C group, which mostly stay below ~900 MPa.

From the pool, the strongest candidates are therefore the ones closest to those top-performing 930°C training samples. In particular:

- **c081** is very close to the best observed 1144 MPa sample, differing mainly in TT = 200 instead of 160.
- **c053, c063, c016, c018** all lie in the same high-performing 930°C / DT850 family and are near training rows with targets around 1030–1110 MPa.

Final: c081, c053, c063, c016, c018
